how-it-was-written.text: Two tables were written independently, then synthesized once. The ticket owner's table has sha256 af9b40091a642895d4f48cfff57c8395654062b44b169f3cd37cbddc48370cae; the table of the gate-author auditor seat (GLM through the pi harness) has sha256 cd2df8ebd9059d99034ebb047ebc25afd5f979e62ffeb4a90a3b322edccb542b. The owner wrote its table before reading the auditor's. Both start from the same acceptance lines (sha256 7a4ab83c5558ef9add3c09cfcc8e83facd9c684a7f0e0f34587da7e9ccb1a438). The auditor read the workflows at base 76bb0993; every command below was read again at e3c9ab01 and then at 24e0c9ba, and once more at 58335316, the base of this branch (the split's approved head); the line numbers are those of 58335316. Against 24e0c9ba the lines of ci.yml after offchain-component-build moved by 43 (the split added the application-separation steps and two jobs for the open-datum package) and the lines of registry.yml after the focused-suite step moved by one; conformance.yml and the first two ci.yml rows did not move; no command or check changed. The one wording change since the auditor's table: edge-unsupported became the model's own edge-inadmissible, because the base now admits two edges only.

commands.text: Local rows run in minutes on a developer machine; hosted rows run only on the pushed head. Minutes are estimates from the job shape and timeout-minutes. A "red run" is a failed GitHub Actions run of that job, the evidence that the command can fail; where none exists in the last eighty failed runs the commit owner shows the focused product RED instead.

acceptance-line-to-commands.text: The PR column says which pull request the line belongs to (1, 2 or both); the commands are the same in both.

gate-additions-at-58335316.text: Three rows added in v1.2, none replacing a settled one. Each is the verbatim command of an existing job at 58335316. They are the ticket owner's own rows: neither gate-author table could cover them, because the jobs did not exist (the open-datum jobs) or the step was not read as a gate row (the separation pair).
